original_txt: Developers - Veil - AV Evasion Primary Menu Veil \xe2\x80\x93 Framework Search for: Follow me on Twitter My Tweets Recent Posts Least Privilege \xe2\x80\x93 Removing Unnecessary Memory Permissions Veil 3.0 Command Line Usage Veil 3.0 Release February 2016 V-Day A Perl of Hope \xe2\x80\x93 January V-Day 2016 Recent Comments zitstifzitstif on Least Privilege \xe2\x80\x93 Removing Unnecessary Memory Permissions Antivirus software -how it works and how to evade it \xe2\x80\x93 00rules on Veil-Evasion How Antivirus Software Works & How to Evade It | Badshaa on Veil-Evasion Ian Keith Armstrong on Veil-Evasion Adventures in Anti-Virus Evasion \xe2\x80\x94 GracefulSecurity on Guides/Videos Skip to content Veil \xe2\x80\x93 Framework The Veil-Framework The Veil-Framework is a collection of red team security tools that implement various attack methods focused on evading detection. It currently consists of: Veil-Evasion: a tool to generate antivirus-evading payloads using a variety of techniques and languages Veil-Catapult: a psexec-style payload delivery system that integrates Veil-Evasion Veil-Pillage: a\xc2 modular post-exploitation framework\xc2 that integrates Veil-Evasion Veil-PowerView: a powershell tool to gain network situational awareness on Windows domains The Veil-Framework is located at\xc2 https://github.com/Veil-Framework/, and the framework superproject is at\xc2 https://github.com/Veil-Framework/Veil/\xc2 which we recommend most users use. This will pull down stable branches of each tool and update them appropriately. 5 thoughts on \xe2\x80\x9cThe Veil-Framework\xe2\x80\x9d jared says: June 25, 2013 at 11:13 am excellent tool. I wonder if there would be a way to pad the encoded part to produce an overall file with lower entropy. Heuristics scanners may pick up on the PE high entropy part of the file, warranting unnecessary attention. http://corte.si/posts/visualisation/malware/ http://deadhacker.com/2007/05/13/finding-entropy-in-binary-files/ Reply CTruncer says: June 26, 2013 at 3:54 pm Valid point, would be worth us looking into. If you have any suggestions, or can create a poc, we\xe2\x80\x99d be interested in seeing something too Reply Jerji says: January 1, 2015 at 6:07 pm I love this tool but would it be possible to include a reverse http hop payload? Reply Nerishi says: July 29, 2015 at 12:38 pm Hey guys, Can\xe2\x80\x99t tell you how much I love the work this project represents, and the superb quality of effort that\xe2\x80\x99s gone into making it work by the team. I wouldn\xe2\x80\x99t bother commenting otherwise. But\xe2\x80\xa6 Does the project need help with documentation? If so, can I help? What would I need to bring to the table to be of practical use? It looks like as the project evolved, your documentation became a bit inconsistent with itself. Minor things like directing us to run \xe2\x80\x9c./setup.sh\xe2\x80\x9d when that file might have become \xe2\x80\x9c./Install.sh\xe2\x80\x9d over time, or deprecating Catapult in favour of Pillage, but the main README.md for the \xe2\x80\x9cVeil\xe2\x80\x9d superproject still references Catapult \xe2\x80\x93 and so on. I feel certain this must lead to lots of (possibly?) needless support requests. Again, I\xe2\x80\x99m not here to beat you up over this; I looove the project, and want to help. Much love for giving back, guys, Nerishi Reply Christopher Truncer says: July 29, 2015 at 10:33 pm Hey there, that would definitely be really helpful. If you\xe2\x80\x99d like, shoot me an e-mail and we can talk about it. Reply Leave a Reply Cancel reply Proudly powered by WordPress ~ Theme: Scrawl by WordPress.com.
